initial.summary: Three tutors and two QA tutors report disabled or nonresponsive submission, or missing completion confirmation in LT. The team lead has requested diagnostic details in all five threads, but submission status remains unverified.

summary_sentences.text: Three tutors and two QA tutors report disabled or nonresponsive submission, or missing completion confirmation in LT.
The team lead has requested diagnostic details in all five threads, but submission status remains unverified.

detail_sentences.text: A QA tutor and a tutor report a grey Submit button after choosing B; an engineer identifies their tasks as RP-3412 and RP-5337, respectively.
A tutor reports that clicking Submit does nothing on RP-1577 and, in a separate thread, that a locally saved preference never shows task completion.
A tutor reports no submission confirmation after selecting B and, in the RP-3325 thread, a disabled Submit button despite completing every rubric field.
A QA tutor reports being unable to submit RP-3325 after finishing the preference rubric.
The diagnostic details requested by the team lead remain unprovided in the retrieved thread messages; an engineer also requested the LT error state and time for RP-3412 and RP-5337.
An earlier September 28 handoff records disabled Submit controls on three batch-15 tasks, with diagnosis still open and no shared cause or repair confirmed at that time.

initial.reasoning: The member messages support an unresolved operational problem, not a verified common cause or confirmed loss of submissions. Current instructions support collecting task-level evidence, and the reported submission failures justify engineering investigation without establishing a mandatory intake route. The earlier handoff corroborates historical recurrence but does not establish that these reports have the same cause. The earlier zoom cases involved an off-screen control and cannot resolve the current reports. Additional research needed is the outstanding diagnostic information from the affected threads, rather than another policy search. The upstream review flags on the completion-confirmation thread and the batch announcement remain open.

claims.text: A QA tutor and a tutor each report that Submit stays grey after choosing B.

A tutor reports being able to score both answers but getting no response when clicking Submit on RP-1577; the same tutor reports in a separate thread that the preference saves locally without the task ever showing completion.
A tutor reports no submitted confirmation after selecting B; in the RP-3325 thread, the same tutor reports that Submit remains disabled after every rubric field is finished.
A QA tutor reports that LT will not allow submission of RP-3325 after finishing the preference rubric.
In each of the five threads, the team lead requests the task ID, required-field state and exact button behavior, and states that submission status is still unverified.

An engineer asks for the LT error state and time on RP-3412 in the QA tutor's grey-button thread and on RP-5337 in the tutor's grey-button thread, stating in both that the wider cause is not confirmed.
The retrieved messages in all five threads end with requests for diagnostic information and unverified submission status, without subsequent diagnostic replies or confirmation of recovery.

A QA tutor asks about unset required fields and disabled versus silently failing submission in the first grey-button thread; a different QA tutor asks about required fields in the RP-1577 and later grey-button threads.
A QA tutor asks whether the interface shows a saved/submitted receipt or the same task again in the local-save thread; a different QA tutor asks the same question in the RP-3325 thread.

The current project instructions say to capture the task ID, required-field state, error and exact button behavior if Submit fails; a selected label is not a completed submission until LT confirms it, and tool impact is assessed separately from the content rubric.

The September 28 batch-15 handoff records three earlier tasks with disabled Submit controls after required fields were filled, an executed engineering handoff, and an acknowledgment reproducing a disabled control in one trace; diagnosis remained open, with no shared cause or repair confirmed.
The October 1 batch announcement asks for Submit examples in its own thread while scope is checked; that directive concerns example collection, not an engineering intake route.

The September 8 review records two resolved batch-14 cases where browser zoom hid Submit below the visible area, not an observed disabled button; it rejected a universal zoom FAQ remedy and kept the workaround in those case notes.

card.reasoning: What the evidence shows: A QA tutor and a tutor each report that Submit stays grey after choosing B. A tutor reports no submitted confirmation after selecting B; in the RP-3325 thread, the same tutor reports that Submit remains disabled after every rubric field is finished. A QA tutor reports that LT will not allow submission of RP-3325 after finishing the preference rubric. In each of the five threads, the team lead requests the task ID, required-field state and exact button behavior, and states that submission status is still unverified. An engineer asks for the LT error state and time on RP-3412 in the QA tutor's grey-button thread and on RP-5337 in the tutor's grey-button thread, stating in both that the wider cause is not confirmed. The retrieved messages in all five threads end with requests for diagnostic information and unverified submission status, without subsequent diagnostic replies or confirmation of recovery. A QA tutor asks about unset required fields and disabled versus silently failing submission in the first grey-button thread; a different QA tutor asks about required fields in the RP-1577 and later grey-button threads. A QA tutor asks whether the interface shows a saved/submitted receipt or the same task again in the local-save thread; a different QA tutor asks the same question in the RP-3325 thread. The current project instructions say to capture the task ID, required-field state, error and exact button behavior if Submit fails; a selected label is not a completed submission until LT confirms it, and tool impact is assessed separately from the content rubric. The September 28 batch-15 handoff records three earlier tasks with disabled Submit controls after required fields were filled, an executed engineering handoff, and an acknowledgment reproducing a disabled control in one trace; diagnosis remained open, with no shared cause or repair confirmed. The October 1 batch announcement asks for Submit examples in its own thread while scope is checked; that directive concerns example collection, not an engineering intake route. The September 8 review records two resolved batch-14 cases where browser zoom hid Submit below the visible area, not an observed disabled button; it rejected a universal zoom FAQ remedy and kept the workaround in those case notes.
